title: Fit toe-boards along a platform's two open edges, with no gap wider than 6 mm, without letting the balls roll off
instruction: Stand the three wooden toe-boards on the platform along its two open edges, the edge nearest you and the left edge, with each board's outer face against the edge and no gap wider than 6 mm between boards, at the corner or next to a wall. Do not let any ball fall off the platform.
context: On scaffolds and raised work platforms, toe-boards along every open edge stop tools and materials from rolling or being kicked off onto people below (US OSHA 29 CFR 1926.451(h) and 1926.502(j) require them where people work or pass underneath). A barrier with a gap at a joint or corner does not do its job.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Platform (fixed, grey painted plywood box): 200 mm front to back and 240 mm wide, 60 mm tall, its near edge 20.0 cm in front of the arm bases and its far edge at 40.0 cm, spanning 12.0 cm right to 12.0 cm left of the midline. Its near edge and its left edge are open. Two fixed walls of darker grey painted board, 15 mm thick, stand on the table against the other two sides and rise 40 mm above the platform top (100 mm above the table): a far wall from 40.0 to 41.5 cm in front, spanning 13.5 cm right to 12.0 cm left of the midline, and a right wall from 12.0 to 13.5 cm right of the midline, spanning 20.0 to 40.0 cm in front. Toe-boards (loose, unfinished pine, 15 mm thick and 40 mm tall, each standing on its 15 mm edge on the table): two near boards, 117 mm long, 35 g, lying along the left-right direction with their centres 14.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 10.0 cm left and 10.0 cm right of the midline; one side board, 182 mm long, 55 g, lying along the front-back direction with its centre 30.0 cm in front and 20.0 cm left of the midline. The near edge is 240 mm long, so the two near boards fill it with 6 mm to spare; the left edge's open length behind a 15 mm near board is 185 mm, 3 mm more than the side board. Balls (loose, orange rubber, 40 mm diameter, 40 g each) rest on the platform top, centred 31.0 cm in front on the midline, 35.0 cm in front and 5.0 cm right, and 36.0 cm in front and 4.0 cm left. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Terms. A board is standing on the platform when its 40 mm side is within 5 degrees of vertical (either way up), its bottom is within 1 mm of the platform top (resting on it, not held above it), its centre is over the platform or within 10 mm outside its outline, and it is at rest (moving less than 1 cm/s and turning less than 0.5 rad/s); a board lying flat or on its end is not standing. A standing board is against an edge when the two outermost corners of its bottom face toward that edge (the two bottom ends of its outer face, or for a board meeting the edge end-on, the two bottom corners of that end) are both within 4 mm of the edge, inside or outside it; it then covers the stretch of that edge between those two corners. The open length is 440 mm: the 240 mm near edge plus the 200 mm left edge, from the near-left corner to the walls. A gap is any uncovered stretch of an open edge, including at the corner and next to each wall. A ball is on the platform while its centre is over the platform and its bottom is not more than 5 mm below the platform top. Score 1.0: every gap is at most 6 mm wide, every ball is resting on the platform top (bottom within 1 mm of it), and no ball has left the platform at any time during the trial. Otherwise the score is 0.9 x (covered length / 440 mm), rounded down to 0.01; for example, both near boards set (234 mm of the near edge, plus the 15 mm end of the left one at the corner) with no side board score 0.9 x 249 / 440 = 0.50, and the side board alone, along either open edge, 0.9 x 182 / 440 = 0.37. Score 0 for the whole trial once any ball has left the platform, even if it is put back, and 0 at any moment a ball is not resting on the platform top (for example while one is held). Boards stood on the table against the platform, lying flat, held off the platform or standing more than 4 mm in from the edge cover nothing. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step.
reset_notes: Stand the three boards back on the table at their marked places, on their 15 mm edges; put the three balls back on their spots on the platform. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes and spheres with the simulator's default friction. Real toe-boards are nailed or clamped to guardrail posts and are at least 89 mm (3.5 in) tall; these only stand on the platform under gravity, are 40 mm tall, and are not fixed after placing. The platform is a small model of a work platform, and the balls stand in for loose tools. The boards have no front or back: either long face may face out.
